## Attack surfaces

- Profile activation and default-reactor exclusion; Maven dependency resolution, Java 8 production bytecode, Java 11 test compilation, and JUnit discovery.
- Concrete triggers that let missing/mismatched IDs or empty test classes silently pass; duplicate IDs across files and Surefire file-name discovery.
- Assurance v2 finalization, required-gate handling, promotion eligibility, and SHA-256 coverage of every promoted copy.
- Consistency between every added workflow MUST/MUST NOT and the actual scripts, POMs, CI job, and agent instructions.
- Context isolation between implementation, isolated test generation, assurance promotion, and independent review.
- The C-0001 public contract and whether its assertions can detect the opposite behavior.
- R4 renamed only the Python verifier test class; confirm no discovery or assertion regression.

## Assurance classification requiring independent confirmation

The initial commit records `assurance: SKIPPED` because production behavior and existing behavioral
evidence are unchanged, and the workflow/test additions do not weaken, remove, or replace existing
evidence. Confirm or reject this against `.agents/skills/project-delivery/references/assurance.md`
and the complete diff. A question or rejection upgrades the run to required.

The earlier review of a pre-rebase snapshot timed out twice and produced no findings; it supplies no
clean baseline. Refactoring review settled R1 as deferred, R2 as reverted for excess growth, R3 as
rejected, and R4 as applied. Do not treat a timed-out review as evidence.

summary: Review found two assurance-integrity defects: the metadata checker can accept a C-class with no executable JUnit test, and the run verifier can accept a claimed promotion without its required archived copy. These possible silent successes mean the recorded assurance skip cannot be confirmed.

findings.title: Lexical @Test detection accepts hollow contract classes
findings.trigger: Add a correctly named and tagged C0002<Subject>ContractTest whose body contains a block-comment line beginning with @Test but declares no test method. The existing C0001 test remains in the module.
findings.consequence: The metadata check succeeds and Surefire still succeeds by running C0001, while C0002 contributes no executable regression coverage. A later behavior regression covered only by C0002 can therefore pass CI.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-contract-tests.py:14 searches raw source text without removing comments or associating the annotation with the C-class, and :47-48 accepts any match. verification/contract-tests/pom.xml:58-60 only rejects a module with zero discovered tests, not an individual hollow class.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a Java parser or post-Surefire XML validation to require at least one non-skipped org.junit.jupiter.api.Test method on each matched C-class. Do not treat annotations in comments, strings, unrelated nested types, shadow annotations, or disabled tests as evidence.

findings.title: Verifier accepts claimed promotions without archived copies
findings.trigger: A run records a candidate as promoted in promotion-status.csv, hashes that CSV, leaves promotions/ empty, and has passing ordinary required gates and Final gate: PASS.
findings.consequence: The verifier accepts a passing assurance run even though no adapted promoted test is retained or SHA-256-bound to the claimed C-nnnn result. The promotion cannot be independently reproduced or audited as required.
findings.evidence: verify_run.py:237-248 verifies hashes only for files that already happen to exist under promotions/ and never reads promotion-status.csv. Phase seven requires each eligible promotion to save its adapted test under RUN_DIR/promotions/ in .agents/skills/contract-first-assurance/SKILL.md:345-354.
findings.suggestedFix: Define a machine-readable promotion-status schema and validate it in verify_run.py. For every promoted row, require a referenced file under promotions/, a verified artifact hash, and the recorded target identity; reject a passing final gate when any claimed promotion lacks this evidence.
